messages:
lina: quick heads-up — a couple of enterprise customers flagged quotas >100% in Console when using cross-project API keys. appears after the metrics pipeline change last week.

alex: can you paste an example request that reproduces?

lina: sure, from staging:

```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Headers: {
  Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-abcd,
  x-redwood-org: org_777,
  x-redwood-project: proj_333,
  x-forwarded-for: 10.0.0.1
}
Body: {"input": "hello"}
```

Observed emitted series: quota.count{owner=org_777} + quota.count{token_origin=sk-prod-abcd} — console sums both into total.

jin: yup. pipeline intentionally emits both owner tagging and token_origin for debugging. console aggregation was naive and now double-counts when both are present. the recent query engine change made console stop preferring the canonical owner tag.

maria: for billing and SLOs we need a single canonical owner per request. proposal: pipeline emits owner_attr with values "project:proj_333", "org:org_777", or "legacy:key:sk-prod-abcd". leave token_origin emitted but mark as debug=false/true flag so console can exclude it from rollups by default.

sam: compact enum is good — reduces cardinality vs emitting full token string in primary key. pipeline cost impact?

jin: adding owner_attr is cheap (small enum). emitting token_origin as debug will keep it available without affecting billing. downside: mapping legacy keys to orgs/projects requires lookup for older keys when available.

alex: historical charts need a story. we cannot reprocess months of raw events cheaply. we should implement a query-time mapping: when owner_attr missing, join the attribution service to resolve tokens to owner_attr and show a migration badge on graphs.

maria: UX detail: show a "canonical attribution" toggle in Console. Default view = canonical (owner_attr). Expand breakdowns to show token_origin only when user opts into raw dimensions. Add a small orange "beta" pill for the first 7 days of rollout.

lina: agree. also add an explanation link for CS: "Why my usage changed" so billing teams get context.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: telemetry-owner-attr-mapper -> canary-2 (5% traffic).

jin: test plan: 1) synthetic request with project header should produce owner_attr=project:proj_333 and only one quota.count series increments; 2) legacy-key request w/o project header produces owner_attr=legacy:key:sk-xxx and is excluded from billing rollups; 3) query-time resolution returns consistent totals for mixed time ranges.

sam: i'll add migration checklist to the runbook and estimate cost delta — approx +10-15% ETL CPU for canary window.

observability-bot: created ticket: RB-402 for runbook updates. Alert 'quota-attr-inconsistency' muted until 1699092000 by lina.

alex: important: ensure invoices are stable. billing queries must keep previous totals for at least 30 days via a compatibility view. Add a `billing_view=compat` flag to queries behind the scenes for invoice generation.

maria: good catch. I'll document billing_view behavior and add tests in billing suite.

jin: I'll open the pipeline PR with change and unit tests. ping @maria @sam for review.

lina: UX engineers — we need the migration badge and toggle by EOD tomorrow for the canary.

maria: assigning frontend PR to alex, backend to jin. target: canary in 48h, promote after 72h stable.

alex: will do. adding small visual indicator: graphs with mixed pre-/post-owner_attr data show "mixed attribution" tooltip.

sam: after canary, run a 1-week reconciliation job: compare canonical totals vs legacy totals and surface any discrepancies >0.5% to billing owners.

maria: thanks team. posting PR links in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
